title: Trofie al Pesto
subtitle: Ligurian pasta with potato, green beans, and pesto
excerpt: The Ligurian way: short pasta cooked alongside potato and green beans, then tossed with a loose, bright pesto genovese. The potato and pasta finish in the same water, and the pesto stays raw.

recipe.sourceNotes: Trofie al pesto is the canonical Ligurian pasta dish: short, hand-rolled pasta served with pesto genovese, potato, and green beans all cooked in the same pot. The potato absorbs the pesto beautifully and the green beans add freshness. Trofie are traditionally hand-rolled in Liguria; penne or fusilli work as substitutes.

recipeTools.notes: Big enough for pasta, potato, and beans together.

content.text: The Ligurian version of pesto pasta is not a sauce poured over pasta. The potato goes into the boiling water first, then the pasta, then the green beans in the last few minutes, so all three finish cooking together. The pesto is made with a generous amount of basil and good oil, kept raw and bright, and tossed with the hot pasta at the last moment.

Make the pesto: blend the basil, pine nuts, garlic, and salt in a food processor. Add the parmesan and pecorino. With the motor running, pour in the olive oil until you have a smooth, vibrant green sauce. Taste and adjust with more salt or oil.
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add the potato cubes and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the pasta to the pot with the potato. Cook according to the packet time. In the last 3 minutes, add the green beans.

Reserve a cup of pasta water. Drain everything together. Transfer to a large warm bowl. Add the pesto and toss, loosening with a little pasta water until the sauce coats everything evenly. Serve with extra grated parmesan.
